title: Samsung Galaxy wearable heart-rate and ECG recordings supporting arrhythmia diagnosis and treatment
summary: Galaxy Fit recorded a resting pulse of 188 bpm; a routine ECG next day showed WPW and the band's records supported referral for successful ablation (South Korea, 2020).
account: On 18 June 2020 a 26-year-old woman working 12-hour days in a multinational company's quality control department in South Korea experienced severe palpitations for hours. Her Samsung Galaxy Fit (SM-R370), which measures pulse by photoplethysmography, recorded a peak resting pulse rate of 188 bpm. The next day, 19 June 2020, a routine health-examination 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) was taken while she was asymptomatic. It showed a shortened PR interval and delta waves, establishing Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome. The authors are from the Department of Occupational and Environmental Medicine at Kangbuk Samsung Hospital. They recommended electrophysiology study based on the ECG, her symptoms and the pulse records from the band. Electrophysiology study and radiofrequency catheter ablation of the bypass tract followed on 29 June 2020 at the authors' hospital. After discharge she monitored for recurrence with a smartwatch. The case was reported in Annals of Occupational and Environmental Medicine on 24 March 2021. A 2024 report describes a Galaxy Watch 4 ECG capturing polymorphic ventricular tachycardia that led to a vasospastic angina diagnosis.
purpose: The Galaxy Fit's optical sensor is built to track heart rate, and the Galaxy Watch ECG app to record single-lead ECGs for rhythm assessment. The benefit came from those functions.
system: Samsung Galaxy Fit heart-rate monitor and Galaxy Watch ECG app
model_version: Galaxy Fit SM-R370 (event); Galaxy Watch Series 4 in echo

ratings.reason: A young worker's band documented a 188 bpm tachycardia. With a routine ECG showing WPW the next day and her symptoms, it backed referral for electrophysiology study. Successful radiofrequency catheter ablation came 11 days after the recorded episode. A material benefit to one person, though the diagnosis itself came from the routine ECG.

ai_role.statement: The band's heart-rate algorithm recorded the 188 bpm episode that documented the tachycardia. Clinicians diagnosed WPW on a 12-lead ECG and performed the ablation. The echo relied on the Galaxy Watch ECG app's trace, read by cardiologists.

evidence.citation: Mun E, Hong J, Kwon S, Lee SH, Kim W, Lee C (2021). Digital health care and arrhythmia: a case of WPW syndrome in South Korea, 2020. Annals of Occupational and Environmental Medicine 33:e8. (Authors at Kangbuk Samsung Hospital, Sungkyunkwan University School of Medicine; hospital staff, not Samsung Electronics.)
evidence.title: Digital health care and arrhythmia: a case of WPW syndrome in South Korea, 2020
evidence.quote: her peak resting pulse rate reached 188 beats per minute

evidence.citation: Avidan Y, Tabachnikov V, Danon A, Schliamser JE (2024). Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia Detected by a Smartwatch in a Patient With Recurrent Syncope. JACC: Case Reports.
evidence.title: Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia Detected by a Smartwatch in a Patient With Recurrent Syncope
evidence.quote: After 1 year of outpatient follow-up, there were no further clinical events.

evidence.citation: Bogár B et al. (2024). Detection of Arrhythmias Using Smartwatches—A Systematic Literature Review. Healthcare 12(9):892.
evidence.title: Detection of Arrhythmias Using Smartwatches—A Systematic Literature Review
evidence.quote: Samsung Galaxy Fit was used for arrhythmia registration in one patient.

produced_by: The wearer uses a Samsung Galaxy band or watch with heart-rate tracking or the ECG app
A symptomatic arrhythmia occurs while the device is worn and the reading or trace is shown to a clinician
A clinician confirms the rhythm and treats it
must_hold: The device recording is reviewed promptly
A 12-lead ECG or inpatient monitoring is available for confirmation
Definitive therapy (ablation, drugs, device) is accessible

echoes.setting: 54-year-old male recreational athlete, Haifa, Israel (authors' institution); Galaxy Watch 4 single-lead ECG during syncope showed polymorphic VT; vasospastic angina with coronary disease, verapamil and wearable defibrillator, no events at one year (publication date)
echoes.source: Avidan et al. (2024). JACC Case Rep. https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11522799

paired_incident.title: Apple Devices Mistook Skiing Activities, Dialed False Distress Emergency Calls
paired_incident.basis: No Samsung wearable incident exists; the nearest wearable false alarm is Apple Watch Crash Detection misclassifying skiing and dialing 911, harming watch users and dispatchers, the inverse of a Galaxy Fit's true 188 bpm detection.

headline: Galaxy Fit pulse of 188 bpm leads to WPW diagnosis and ablation
metric: recorded a peak resting pulse rate of 188 beats per minute

later.note: After catheter ablation on 29 June 2020 the patient kept using a smartwatch to monitor for recurrence, as the case report published in March 2021 records.
later.quote: She received EPS on June 29 at our hospital, and radio frequency catheter ablation was simultaneously conducted to eliminate the bypass tract. Since her discharge, she has kept monitoring symptom recurrence with a smartwatch.
